subject: Post-call recap: Paylane discovery — batching & cache levers, ROI and procurement timeline
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aditi Singh <aditi@paylane.com>, Tom Berger <tom.berger@paylane.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call recap: Paylane discovery — batching & cache levers, ROI and procurement timeline

Thanks for your time today — quick recap and where we land on next steps. Short version up front: Paylane sees 3x token spend growth if you go live with current chat volume and plan; we scoped a 6-week pilot that uses batching + prefix cache to cut token bill 30–45% while keeping 90th p99 latency SLOs, and finance needs a scoped SOW + 1 pager ROI to kick procurement.

Key pain points you shared:
- High per-transaction token spend on multi-turn chat flows (esp. refunds & disputes).
- Tight Q3 budget window; procurement needs a clear cost-savings projection and pilot definition.
- Security: SOC2 evidence + IP isolation required before production.

What we proposed on the call:
- Pilot scope: 6 weeks, non-prod routing + 100k monthly token baseline simulation, measure accuracy + cost delta.
- Technical levers: continuous batching (client-side + server-side), prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, and a lower-cost quantized model for low-risk flows.
- Metrics to measure: tokens saved (%), token cost per API call, end-to-end p95 latency, and accuracy drift vs baseline.

Preliminary economics (high level):
- Baseline monthly token cost (stated): ~$42k
- Conservative pilot expectation: 30% token reduction => ~$12.6k/mo saved (pilot extrapolation)
- Upside w/ aggressive caching: up to 45% => ~$18.9k/mo saved
- Estimated Redwood pilot cost (6-week): $8k–$12k depending on reserved capacity config (detailed numbers in attached SOW draft).

Immediate asks from Paylane:
1) Finance: an ROI one-pager + pilot SOW to circulate to procurement (you mentioned EOD Fri).
2) Engineering: list of 3 example endpoints to route through pilot (refunds, dispute triage, agent-assist).
3) Security: list of SOC2 artifacts and proposed network isolation model.

Next steps / owners:
- Ben: deliver ROI one-pager + SOW draft by Thu EOD (attached SOW draft).
- Marissa: align on commercial terms and pilot pricing options (in thread).
- Aditi/Tom: share finance contact and preferred procurement timeline; send sample traffic endpoints.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-sow-draft.pdf (pdf, 2 pages)

--
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0112

From: Aditi Singh <aditi@paylane.com>

Cc: Tom Berger <tom.berger@paylane.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 16:45:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Paylane discovery — batching & cache levers, ROI and procurement timeline

Thanks Ben — this is great and matches our notes. A few clarifications and constraints from my side:

- Baseline numbers: the $42k/month is the combined production + staging estimate for the 3 chat endpoints. Production traffic is ~70% of that.
- Budget gate: procurement will only approve spend that shows <6mo payback on recurring savings. That’s a hard requirement from finance.
- Security: SOC2 Type II report + encrypted key management are must-haves. We can give a restricted S3 bucket for logs during pilot.

I attached a trimmed budget spreadsheet with our expected Q3 budget ceiling — call it paylane-budget-2026.xlsx. Finance wants an ROI one-pager that shows conservative and optimistic scenarios and the break-even point.

Action from us:
- I’ll send examples of the refund + dispute endpoints by Thu morning.
- Procurement contact: sara.morris@paylane.com — she handles pilots and contract routing.

On timing: if we can get the SOW + ROI by Thu EOD, procurement can review next week and potentially sign off within that 2–3 week window. That meets our internal Q3 planning.

Attachments: paylane-budget-2026.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Best,
Aditi Singh
Head of Product, Paylane
aditi@paylane.com

Aditi — thanks for the budget file, attached is the ROI one-pager and updated SOW draft. I pulled conservative and aggressive scenarios based on the traffic profile you gave in the sheet. Highlights below, full math in the ROI doc: 

Pilot sizing summary:
- Pilot window: 6 weeks (4 weeks data collection + 2 weeks ramp)
- Routing: non-prod namespace with mirrored traffic ~100k monthly tokens simulated (you recommended this to reduce customer impact)
- Reserved capacity options: small reserved pool (2 GPUs) vs burstable (no reserve) — price delta ~ $3.5k over 6 weeks

Updated econ (monthly projection if scaled to prod):
- Conservative: 30% token reduction => $12.6k/mo saved => 4.2mo payback (pilot + integration costs included)
- Optimistic: 40% reduction => $16.8k/mo saved => 3.1mo payback

Given procurement rule (<6mo), conservative scenario clears finance. We also call out a mid-pilot checkpoint at week 3 to validate assumptions and pause/rescope if savings <20%.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-sow-draft.pdf (updated 2 pages), paylane-roi-onepager.pdf (one-pager)

Next asks:
- Aditi/Tom: confirm procurement contact (Sara) and preferred contract vehicle (PO vs SOW + invoice).
- Marissa: will you confirm list price options for the reserved vs burstable pilot?

If we get confirmation today, I can route the SOW for signature and have our legal team prepare a 30-day pilot amendment.

Thanks —
Ben
